question: What objection arises if an object's luminosity is treated as its own power or property?
premises: An opponent may claim that when knowledge arises, the object becomes manifest.
The opponent may treat that manifestness as the object's own power or property.
If every object had such a property, universal omniscience would follow.
inference: Making luminosity an intrinsic property of objects leads to the absurd consequence of omniscience throughout the world.
plain_english: But if, when knowledge arises, that luminosity of the object is its own power or property, then omniscience would follow throughout the whole universe.
